title: TermsUpdateDialog
wrapsNative: sheet(isPresented:) with interactiveDismissDisabled for the blocking form, holding a ScrollView with Text, Text(date, format:), Link with buttonStyle(.monarchLink(.standalone, isExternal: true)), MonarchInlineNotice for an error and MonarchButton for accept and decline
summary: A recipe, not a component: a sheet that tells people the terms have changed, with a summary, the effective date and links to the documents, which in its blocking form cannot be dismissed until they accept or decline.
whenToUse: When updated terms or a privacy policy must be shown at sign-in or on launch, either to be accepted (blocking) or only to inform.
whenNotToUse: For consent to optional processing such as analytics use the consent recipes (see cookie-consent-banner). For a minor wording change, a banner (MonarchBanner) is enough.
api: func sheet(isPresented: Binding<Bool>, content: () -> some View) -> some View

states.name: blocking
states.description: Accept and continue, and Decline (for example Sign out); the sheet cannot be swiped away.

states.name: informational
states.description: One Got it button; the sheet can be swiped away.

states.name: pending
states.description: The accept button shows its loading state and dismissal stays disabled while the acceptance is recorded.

states.name: error
states.description: A danger MonarchInlineNotice above the buttons when recording the acceptance failed.

appearance: A system sheet on the theme's surface colour with the title in the heading style, body text in the default and muted text colours, links in the link colour with the external icon, a primary accept button and a ghost decline button.
platformNotes: The web TermsUpdateDialog is a component with mode, effectiveDate parsing, documents, version labels and pending and error props. On iOS it composes a sheet: the date is formatted with Text(date, format:) in the person's locale, links open in the browser through the environment's openURL, and blocking is interactiveDismissDisabled. Android plans the same recipe.
accessibility: The title has the header trait; VoiceOver focus moves into the sheet when it appears.
Each document is a Link, read with "opens in the browser" from the Monarch link style.
The accept button reads its loading state; an error is shown as text in a notice with an icon, not only colour.
In the blocking form the escape gesture does nothing, so decline must be offered as a button.
edgeCases: At the largest text sizes the summary and links scroll; keep the buttons under the ScrollView so they stay visible.
Show the sheet once per version: store the accepted version and compare on launch.
If declining signs the person out, say so on the decline button.
